prompt:
A cyclist and bicycle have a combined mass of 75.0 kg and travel along a straight horizontal road. The mechanical rolling friction is constant at 14.0 N. The air resistance D increases with speed: at 4.00 m s^-1, D = 11.0 N; at 10.0 m s^-1, D = 66.0 N. The cyclist pedals to exert a constant forward driving force of 50.0 N.
(a) Calculate the resultant force and instantaneous acceleration at a speed of 4.00 m s^-1. [2]
(b) Calculate the resultant force and instantaneous acceleration at a speed of 10.0 m s^-1, and explain what happens to the speed of the cyclist. [2]

mark_scheme.criterion: Total resistance at 4.00 m s^-1 = 14.0 + 11.0 = 25.0 N; resultant force F_net = 50.0 - 25.0 = 25.0 N forward.
Total resistance at 10.0 m s^-1 = 14.0 + 66.0 = 80.0 N; resultant force F_net = 50.0 - 80.0 = -30.0 N (backward).
Acceleration = -30.0 / 75.0 = -0.400 m s^-2 (deceleration of 0.400 m s^-2); speed of the cyclist decreases because resistive force exceeds driving force.

hints: Total resistive force is the sum of rolling friction and air resistance.
Resultant force = driving force - total resistive force.
In (b), if resultant force is negative (opposing motion), what happens to speed?
solution:
(a) Total resistance = 14.0 + 11.0 = 25.0 N. F_net = 50.0 - 25.0 = 25.0 N forward. a = 25.0 / 75.0 = 0.333 m s^-2.
(b) Total resistance = 14.0 + 66.0 = 80.0 N. F_net = 50.0 - 80.0 = -30.0 N. a = -30.0 / 75.0 = -0.400 m s^-2. The speed decreases because the resistive force is greater than the driving force.
teacher_walkthrough: For part (a): R_total = 14.0 + 11.0 = 25.0 N. Net forward force = 50.0 - 25.0 = 25.0 N. a = 25.0 / 75.0 = 0.333 m s^-2. Award C1, A1.

For part (b): R_total = 14.0 + 66.0 = 80.0 N. Net force = 50.0 - 80.0 = -30.0 N. a = -30.0 / 75.0 = -0.400 m s^-2. State that cyclist decelerates / slows down because net force opposes motion. Award C1, A1.
